summary: Self-custodial crypto card program whose separate Solana card-balance contract was affected by the August 2026 Rain incident.
Self-custodial neofinance and crypto card program that reported unauthorized withdrawals from Solana card balances during the August 2026 Rain incident and later reported the issue resolved.
Crypto card program that publicly stated it was not affected by the August 2026 incident affecting other card providers.

Crypto-native Visa-compatible card program for spending USDC and other supported stablecoin balances in real-world payments, documented by Solayer as on-chain and non-custodial. Solayer Pay explicitly stated it was not affected by the August 2026 Rain incident.
Self-custodial crypto debit card that lets eligible users spend supported tokens from MetaMask wherever Mastercard is accepted.

Coinbase prepaid debit card for spending cash or converted crypto at merchants that accept Visa debit cards. The current U.S. infrastructure is distinct from the Paysafe-issued UK/EU generation launched in 2019.
Crypto-native credit card product from ether.fi that is designed to work anywhere Visa is accepted.
Self-custodial crypto debit card that lets users spend supported stablecoins from a Gnosis Safe wallet through the Visa network without preloading funds into a custodial card balance.
Digital Visa debit card inside Opera's MiniPay wallet that spends from the user's self-custodial stablecoin balance and is powered by Gnosis Pay.
U.S. Visa Signature credit card integrated with Crypto.com's app and rewards program, distinct from the Crypto.com Prepaid Visa Card.
Crypto-backed Mastercard card launched in Europe in 2022 with a credit-line model and expanded in 2023 with switchable credit and debit modes.
U.S. crypto debit card program funded from the BitPay wallet; BitPay has publicly documented new card applications as temporarily paused while the program is improved.

Region-dependent crypto card program that spends from Bybit account balances. Current Bybit documentation shows Mastercard or Visa variants by region, while the legacy EEA/CH Bybit.com card was directed to transition to the separate Bybit EU Card programme.
U.S. Mastercard rewards credit card from Gemini, publicly launched in April 2022, that spends U.S. dollars while depositing earned rewards in supported cryptocurrencies; issued by WebBank.

Crypto debit card integrated with the Ledger ecosystem and provided by Baanx. Funds transferred from a Ledger wallet to the CL Card account leave self-custody; reviewed U.S. expansion evidence identifies the U.S. card as Visa.
Regionally issued prepaid Visa card distinct from Crypto.com's U.S. Visa Signature credit card. Crypto used to fund the card is converted to fiat, and the issuer structure varies by market.
Separate Bybit EU Mastercard debit-card program funded from a Bybit EU Funding Account and available across selected European markets. It is distinct from the legacy Bybit.com EEA/CH card program.

Region-dependent payment card program connected to Wirex accounts. Current EEA terms identify a Mastercard card issued by Transact Payments Malta Limited and managed by Wirex UAB; Singapore terms identify Wirex Pte Ltd as card issuer.

Visa debit card connected to Bitpanda payment assets. Bitpanda replaced its prior Contis-issued card at the end of March 2025 with a new card issued by Transact Payments Malta Limited from April 2025.

Current U.S. Uphold debit-card program comprising Essential and Elite card plans, issued by Cross River Bank on Visa with Uphold HQ Inc. as program manager. Archived U.S. terms show an earlier Metropolitan Commercial Bank/Mastercard infrastructure generation.

European Binance crypto debit-card program historically issued by UAB Finansinės paslaugos „Contis“ on Visa. Binance confirmed the program would cease to be available from 2023-12-20; the historical first-party card pages were no longer retrievable in this review.

U.S. crypto-rewards credit card marketed by BlockFi, issued by Evolve Bank & Trust and serviced by Deserve. A BlockFi bankruptcy court filing states the card was no longer active after Visa sent a termination letter on 2022-11-16.

Coinbase's first debit-card generation, introduced in November 2015 and issued through payment processor Shift, allowing Coinbase bitcoin balances to be spent wherever Visa was accepted. Coinbase later described this as its initial card generation before Shift pivoted and a new UK Coinbase Card was implemented in 2019.

European Visa debit-card program from Cryptopay. Its prior PayrNet-issued EUR card operations were discontinued after PayrNet lost its EMI licence in June 2023; current terms identify DiPocket as issuer and CPS Europe S.A. as programme manager.

Historical TenX Visa prepaid-card generation issued by Wave Crest Holdings Limited. Non-European WaveCrest cards became unusable from 2017-10-16, and the remaining WaveCrest-issued TenX cards stopped working after WaveCrest's Visa card programs were disabled in January 2018.

Historical Bitwala crypto debit-card generation whose card service was halted in January 2018 after Visa terminated WaveCrest's card-program relationship. This record is distinct from later Bitwala/Nuri and current Bitwala card generations.

Historical European BitPay Visa debit-card program issued by Wave Crest Holdings Ltd. BitPay stated in January 2018 that the European card was no longer available after the WaveCrest shutdown, while U.S. BitPay Card users were unaffected.
